overview: You Only Live Twice is a 1967 spy film and the sixth film in the James Bond series, and the fifth film in the series if the non-Eon Productions Casino Royale is excluded. The film's screenplay was written by Roald Dahl, and was loosely based on Ian Fleming's 1964 novel You Only Live Twice. It is the first of three Bond films to be directed by Lewis Gilbert, and is the first Bond film to discard most of Fleming's plot, using only a few characters and locations from the book as the background for an entirely new story.
